task.title: Footnotes
task.shortdesc: A footnote is an element that CSSMedia moves to the bottom of the page where the text refers to it. In the text, a number takes its place. The footnote reference lists the properties, rules and pseudo-elements used here.

context.p: These terms are used in this chapter:

ul.li: The footnote body is the content of the footnote element.
The footnote call is the number that replaces the footnote in the text.
The footnote marker is the number at the start of the footnote body.
The footnote area is the box at the bottom of the page that holds the footnote bodies.

context.p: The element names in the examples, such as fn, are placeholders. Use the names that occur in your XML.

info.p: CSSMedia removes fn from the text, puts a number in its place, and shows the content of fn in the footnote area of the same page, in document order. If the footnote does not fit on the page, the rest continues on the next pages.
The rule of the footnote element styles the footnote body, so set the font size and the line height there.

Footnotes are numbered with the footnote counter. A counter is a number that CSS keeps for you and that you can show in the content of a document. The footnote counter already exists: CSSMedia creates it at the start of the document with the value 0 and adds 1 each time it finds a footnote. The first footnote is 1, the second is 2, and so on through the whole document.
The call and the marker of a footnote show the same value, because both use counter(footnote).
You change the numbering with the properties counter-reset, counter-set and counter-increment:

ul.li: counter-reset: footnote sets the counter to 0, so the next footnote is 1. counter-reset: footnote 9 sets it to 9, so the next footnote is 10.
counter-set: footnote 4 also sets the value of the counter.
counter-increment: footnote 2 adds 2 to the counter, and counter-increment: footnote -1 subtracts 1.

info.p: Where you write the declaration decides where the numbering changes. In an element rule, it changes when the element starts. This example starts the numbers at 1 in each chapter:
In an @page rule, it changes on every page. This example starts the numbers at 1 on each page:
With the rule in @page, the number of a footnote depends on the page of its call, and a footnote that continues on the next page keeps its number.

The optional second argument of counter() is a counter style, which sets how the number is written. For example, counter(footnote, lower-alpha) shows a, b, c, and counter(footnote, upper-roman) shows I, II, III. A style can also list the symbols to use:
The first three footnotes show *, † and ‡. Write the same style in the call and in the marker.

step.cmd: Style the call and the marker

info.p: The pseudo-element ::footnote-call is the number in the text. The pseudo-element ::footnote-marker is the number at the start of the footnote. By default, the call is the value of the footnote counter as a superscript, and the marker is the value followed by a period and a space.
Use the content property to change what they show. For example, show the number in brackets:

To show a symbol or a label from the XML instead of a number, give the call and the marker that text, and stop the footnote from using a number. Every footnote adds 1 to the counter, and counter-increment: footnote -1 takes it back, so the other footnotes keep their numbers.

info.p: Use an @footnote rule inside an @page rule to style the footnote area. The area sits at the bottom of the page area. A border and a margin separate it from the text.

Set max-height to limit the height of the area, so that a page does not fill up with footnotes. The limit does not apply to a page that has only footnotes. Because @footnote belongs to an @page rule, you can set a different limit for a named page:
The footnote-display property sets how a footnote body appears in the footnote area:

ul.li: block puts each footnote in its own block. This is the initial value.
inline runs the footnotes together in one paragraph.
compact puts footnotes in the same line when they fit, and in separate blocks when they do not.

step.cmd: Choose what happens when a footnote does not fit

info.p: The footnote-policy property sets what CSSMedia does when the body of a footnote does not fit on the page of its call:

ul.li: auto starts the footnote on the page of its call and continues it on the next pages. This is the initial value.
line moves the line that has the call to the next page, together with the footnote. Widows and orphans are respected, so more than one line can move.
block moves the whole paragraph that has the call to the next page, together with the footnote.
